2027-03-06.title: Saturday of the fourth week of the Great Fast
readings: The covenant at Beer-sheba; Abraham calls on the Everlasting God
Everything created by God is good, received with thanksgiving
I must proclaim the good news to the other cities also
2027-03-06.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fourth week. Tomorrow is K'piphtho Sunday, the fifth Sunday of the Great Fast.
2027-03-06.verse: I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose.
theo: The first reading closes the week of Abraham's story with a scene of peace. Abimelech, the same king Abraham once feared, comes to him with the commander of his army and says: “God is with you in all that you do.” A pagan ruler recognizes God's presence in Abraham's life, and asks for a covenant of loyalty. There is still a dispute: Abimelech's servants have seized a well. Wells meant life in that dry land, and quarrels over water were bitter. Abraham does not fight; he sets apart seven ewe lambs as a witness that he dug the well, and the two men swear an oath. The place is named Beer-sheba, the well of the oath or the well of seven. Then, in a land that was not yet his, Abraham “planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God.” A tree takes years to give shade; planting it is an act of hope. Abraham, still “an alien many days in the land of the Philistines,” lives as a guest who trusts that the Everlasting God will keep his promise.

Paul's words to Timothy are especially fitting in the Great Fast. Some false teachers, he says, “forbid marriage and demand abstinence from foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, provided it is received with thanksgiving; for it is sanctified by God’s word and by prayer.” Our fasting is not a rejection of God's good creation. We do not abstain from meat, fish or eggs because they are evil, but because we want to hunger more for God, to share with the poor, and to master our desires. St Basil the Great said that the true fast is to be a stranger to evil: to restrain the tongue, to put away anger, to stop lying and slander; fasting from food without fasting from sin is not enough (in substance). And when the Fast ends, we will receive God's gifts again with thanksgiving. In the Gospel, the crowds want to keep Jesus for themselves, but he says: “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose.” Our Lenten prayer is not meant to make us comfortable in one place. It sends us out, like Jesus, to bring the good news further, to the next village, the next house, the next person who has not heard.
outline: Ask: what do you think fasting is really for?
Point 1 · The well of the oath
Abraham makes peace and plants a tree of hope.
Why we fast from good things.
Point 3 · To the other cities also
Jesus will not be kept in one place.
“I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also.”
live: If there is a dispute in your family or neighbourhood over water, a boundary or money, take one step this week to settle it peacefully.
Give thanks before every meal (1 Timothy 4:4–5)
During the rest of the Fast, never eat without first thanking God, and set aside what you save by fasting for someone in need.
2027-03-06.prayer: Everlasting God, Abraham called on your name under the tamarisk tree at Beer-sheba, a guest in a land that was not yet his. Make us peacemakers who settle quarrels without violence, and pilgrims who plant seeds of hope. Teach us to fast not out of contempt for your good creation but out of hunger for you, and to receive all your gifts with thanksgiving. Send us, like your Son, to bring the good news to the other cities also. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the great thanksgiving: the bread and wine, good gifts of creation, are offered with prayer and become, by the power of the Holy Spirit, the Body and Blood of Christ.

quick: Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant at Beer-sheba, and Abraham called on the name of the Everlasting God.
Everything created by God is good, received with thanksgiving and sanctified by God's word and prayer.
Jesus would not stay in one place: he was sent to proclaim the kingdom to other cities also.
2027-03-06.action: Settle one small quarrel peacefully this week.
2027-03-06.question: Why do I fast, and does my fasting make me more thankful and more generous?

family.explain: After healing many sick people, Jesus went to a quiet place to pray. The people wanted him to stay with them always. But Jesus said: I have to tell the good news about God to other towns too. That is why I was sent. Jesus wants everyone to hear about God's love.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for people who have never heard of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is someone we can tell about Jesus or invite to church?”

illus: In a hamlet near Adoor two families quarrelled for years over a shared well on their boundary. One summer the well nearly dried up. The older of the two fathers, a quiet man who had just come back from a Lenten retreat, called a well-digger, paid to deepen it, and then put up a small board beside it with the names of both families. His wife asked why he put the neighbours' name first. He said: if the water is God's, the order does not matter. That Easter both families carried the same well water to bless their homes.

pm.open: Everlasting God, we call on your name. Make us peacemakers, thankful for your gifts, and send us out with your good news. Amen.
share: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord (Genesis 21:33). What “tree of hope” am I planting for the future?
Everything created by God is good... received with thanksgiving (1 Timothy 4:4). Does my fasting make me more grateful?
I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also (Luke 4:43). Where is Jesus sending me?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out with your good news.
interc: For peace in disputes over water, land and resources.
For farmers and all who depend on rain and wells.
For missionaries and evangelizers, especially in North India.
For the poor who will share the fruits of our fasting.
For our parish as we prepare for K'piphtho Sunday.
pm.close: Father, you are the Everlasting God, faithful to your promises. Make us peacemakers, thankful stewards of your creation, and joyful messengers of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abimelech came to Abraham and said: God is with you in all that you do (Genesis 21:22). When a dispute arose over a well, Abraham did not fight; he made a covenant of peace at Beer-sheba.

Then Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God (Genesis 21:33). A tree is an act of hope. Abraham lived as a guest, trusting God's promise.

Paul reminds us that everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, provided it is received with thanksgiving (1 Timothy 4:4). We do not fast because food is evil. We fast to hunger for God, to master ourselves, and to share with the poor.
And Jesus says: I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose (Luke 4:43). Let our fasting send us out to share the good news. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus did not stay in one town. He said: I must tell the good news to other towns too! Jesus wants everyone in the world to know God loves them. You can help him: tell one friend about Jesus, or invite someone to come to church with you.

intro: Theme: “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also.”
Peace at the well of Beer-sheba, the true meaning of fasting, and Jesus sent to the other cities.

sub: God is with you in all that you do.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.
points.apply: Take one step this week to settle a dispute peacefully.

sub: We fast to hunger for God.
q: O Lord, how manifold are your works! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Pray before every meal for the rest of the Fast and give what you save to the poor.

sub: The crowds want to keep him.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: Invite one person this week to pray with you or to come to the Holy Qurbono.

concl: Abraham made peace, planted hope and called on the Everlasting God.
Fasting with thanksgiving sends us out, like Jesus, with the good news.
2027-03-06.resolve: Fast with a thankful heart, make peace where you can, and share the good news with one person before Easter.
